elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: PB remains subject to predetermined termination-triggered amounts, including 300% of Development Costs under Section 14.2.1, 100% under Section 14.2.2, 150% under Section 14.2.6, and Development Costs plus 25% annual interest under Section 14.2.10. Describing these amounts as consideration for the Trial Data Package does not eliminate their operative payment obligations.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains premium formulas of 300% and 150% of Development Costs and a 25% annual interest uplift, each payable by PB upon specified terminations and potentially penalty-like in operation.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer is an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The clause does not limit liquidated amounts to one defined early-termination fee; it retains several different termination-triggered payment formulas under Sections 14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.6, and 14.2.10.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No three-month-fee cap appears. The amounts are instead calculated by reference to 100%, 150%, or 300% of Development Costs, or Development Costs plus 25% annual interest.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer, with no additional liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause preserves multiple additional termination-triggered amounts and does not state that any one fee is PB's sole liquidated payment obligation.

result.reason: The redline reduces only the Section 14.2.2 formula from 300% to 100% of Development Costs while leaving the 300%, 150%, and 25%-interest formulas operative. It therefore reaches neither the preferred no-damages/no-penalties position nor the fallback three-month sole-fee position. It also changes the payment period to 90 days without that change being needed to satisfy either level. The remaining provisions are generally coherent and unrelated approval-payment mechanics remain effective, but the requested protection is materially incomplete.
